extracted.intended_audience: media scholars, journalism researchers, and newsroom editors
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and factors that influence online news editorial selection and homepage placement, focusing on reader-derived metrics (clicks, dwell time, shares) and newsroom/individual characteristics that shape metric use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrated Click-Through
rubrics_metrics.description: High-performing stories influence selection of related/follow-up coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories that have already attracted clicks are more likely to be chosen for follow-ups or additional related reporting; editors use past click behavior as a signal of audience interest when deciding what to promote next.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-on-Page (Dwell Time)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories where readers stick around longer signal quality and are favored for promotion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Longer time-on-page is treated as a signal of engagement/quality and can increase the likelihood of promotion or homepage placement; used as an operationalizable metric alongside clicks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Click-Through Rate (CTR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Headlines that draw clicks shape future headline-writing and topic selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CTR informs headline and story selection practices — high-CTR headlines/topics are replicated or prioritized; CTR is a measurable outcome that feeds into editorial decisions about framing and prominence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social-Sharing Volume
rubrics_metrics.description: Highly shared stories pull in additional related coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shares on social platforms are read as evidence of broader audience interest and can trigger additional reporting, reposting, or elevated homepage placement; social volume also interacts with promotion strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search Traffic (SEO Strength)
rubrics_metrics.description: SEO-strong stories direct subsequent reporting toward search-discoverable topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories that attract organic search traffic are prioritized because they are discoverable and can sustain readership; search metrics help editors identify topics with ongoing audience demand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real-Time Trending (Real-time Analytics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Real-time analytics (Chartbeat, Parse.ly) can shift homepage placement minute-to-minute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Real-time platforms enable continuous, sub-cycle re-ordering of front-page placement; editors may react quickly to trending signals to promote or demote stories throughout the day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outlet's Economic Model
rubrics_metrics.description: Outlet's economic model (subscriber vs. ad-revenue dependent) influences reliance on metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ad-revenue-dependent outlets tend to be more metric-driven because audience volume directly affects revenue; subscriber-funded or paywalled models may reduce emphasis on raw traffic metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor's Role Identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Editor's self-identification (entrepreneurial vs. traditional) shapes use of audience metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors who see themselves as entrepreneurial are more likely to use metrics as primary inputs for selection, whereas traditionally oriented editors prioritize editorial norms over metric signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalism Training
rubrics_metrics.description: More journalism education and experience correlate with reduced reliance on metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors with stronger journalism training are less inclined to use metrics as the primary selection criterion, suggesting professional norms and training mediate metric influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Years of Experience
rubrics_metrics.description: More experienced editors show less reliance on audience metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experience correlates negatively with metric reliance; experienced editors may lean on judgment, beats, and institutional norms rather than immediate audience signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outlet Size
rubrics_metrics.description: Smaller outlets are more reliant on audience metrics than larger outlets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local and smaller digital-native outlets show greater metric-driven behavior compared with legacy national outlets, potentially due to resource constraints or economic pressures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beat / Topic Area
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain beats (lifestyle/entertainment) are more metric-driven than others (politics/foreign).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topics that naturally attract casual or social traffic (entertainment, lifestyle) are more responsive to metric signals, while hard news beats may be less influenced by short-term audience measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routine Monitoring of Audience Behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: 58% of editors actively monitor audience behavior when checking web traffic — making audience metrics a routine input to selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular monitoring normalizes metrics as part of editorial workflow; routine attention to dashboards means decisions are continually informed by audience data rather than a one-time editorial judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metric-Driven Editorial Actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Watching metrics changes decisions about which stories to promote, repost, push to social media, and run as follow-ups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metrics do not only inform story selection but drive concrete actions — homepage placement, reposting, social pushes, and commissioning follow-ups — creating feedback loops between audience behavior and editorial output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perceived Economic Benefit of Readership
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors who attach high readership to economic benefit are significantly more likely to base selection decisions on metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When editors equate readership increases with economic gain, they are more disposed to prioritize metric-performing stories; perceived monetary value of audience attention conditions metric use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience as Active Gatekeeper
rubrics_metrics.description: Treating the audience as a measured, real-time level of influence in the hierarchy of influences model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vu proposes revising Shoemaker & Reese's hierarchy to add the audience as an active level — not just an imagined audience but a quantified signal that operates alongside individual, organizational, and institutional influences on newsworthiness and selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metric-Driven Re-Prioritization (Continuous Scoring)
rubrics_metrics.description: Real-time analytics enable continuous, sub-cycle re-ordering of front-page placement; newsworthiness becomes a feedback-driven scoring process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection is no longer a one-shot judgment; editors can iteratively re-score and re-order stories based on live engagement metrics, producing dynamic homepage configurations responsive to immediate audience behavior.
